articles.title: 4 bold predictions for the Chargers' defense in 2026
articles.summary: From defensive takeaways to star-studded performances, these four bold predictions showcase how we expect the Chargers' defense to perform in 2026.
articles.body:
The Chargers have a ton going for them as the 2026 season approaches, and much of that has to do with their defense.

Los Angeles has a chance to continue to be one of the league's best defenses under Chris O'Leary, just as they were with Jesse Minter calling the shots over the last two seasons.

The Chargers' defense has a lot on the line, and it's time to put some bold predictions on the table.

4. Daiyan Henley finishes as the Chargers' leading tackler, named Pro Bowler

We're coming in hot with the first one. The first part of that prediction is far from bold, as Henley led the team in tackles last season with 103. The second part is certainly the definition of bold. He's already shown flashes of playing at a Pro Bowl-caliber level. However, in 2026, Henley is expected to step into a definitive leadership role and be the anchor of the middle for the Chargers' defense. If Henley can have it all come together on a week-to-week basis, Henley has a great chance to earn that nod.

3. Genesis Smith quickly emerges as a pillar of the Chargers' secondary

We have to show the rookie some love. Smith, the fourth-round pick, doesn't have to become a superstar overnight for this prediction to hit. Nonetheless, he possesses elite centerfield range, high-upside ball-hawking instincts, and a modern defensive scheme that maximizes his strengths. Smith will have to continue improving in the tackling department, but the coverage skills should allow him to flourish very quickly.

2. The Chargers finish with a top-five scoring defense

The Chargers finished ninth in this area, and with what I believe is an improved unit, personnel-wise, this is well within reach. Los Angeles has enough talent to make a significant jump defensively, and the biggest reason to believe it is the number of playmakers they have at every level. If health is on their side and the young guys develop quickly, the Bolts could go from simply a good defense to one of the NFL's most difficult units to score against.

1. Akheem Mesidor leads the team in sacks

The rookie edge rusher has shown that he can come into the league and make an immediate impact on the Chargers' defense. Mesidor doesn't have the best player on the defensive line, but he does need to take advantage of the opportunities that come with playing alongside established players like Khalil Mack and Tuli Tuipulotu. With Mack and Tuipulotu there, Mesidor could likely benefit from more favorable one-on-one matchups. If he can take advantage of that, there's a realistic path to him leading the team in sacks. In his final college season, Mesidor had 12.5 sacks.

articles.title: ‘Even my wife is watching’: Srikkanth says Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is making cricket exciting again
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Former India opener Kris Srikkanth believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has the potential to become one of the biggest names in world cricket, wit.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Former India opener Kris Srikkanth believes Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has the potential to become one of the biggest names in world cricket, with the teenage sensation already generating an unusual level of excitement around the game.Sooryavanshi, just 15, has continued his rapid rise by making a mark in the Duleep Trophy after already setting the IPL and international stages alight. For Srikkanth, however, the youngster's impact is going beyond numbers — he is making people tune in to cricket they might otherwise have overlooked.“He's playing outstandingly well. He must be encouraged and never be discouraged. If he's moulded properly, he'll be a superstar in the making. He'll bring Test cricket back to its glory. Everyone watched the Duleep Trophy because of him. Even my wife is watching because of him. He'll be a big asset going forward for World cricket,” Srikkanth said on his YouTube channel.‘He’ll be a superstar in the making’Sooryavanshi has certainly given fans plenty to watch. After failing to make an impact in East Zone's quarterfinal win over North East Zone, he responded emphatically against Central Zone in the semifinal.The teenager smashed 92 off 81 balls in the first innings and then contributed a crucial 40 in the final innings as East Zone secured a four-wicket victory to book their place in the final.At 15 years and 157 days, Sooryavanshi had already become the youngest batter to score a half-century in Duleep Trophy history, breaking a 57-year-old record.Srikkanth was particularly impressed by the teenager's fearless approach in red-ball cricket and believes there is little reason to question his ability to make the jump to the highest level.“He played incredibly well. How can people even doubt whether this boy on whether he is capable of playing higher-level cricket? He can play every level of cricket, and he is going to rule world cricket shortly in all formats. He's smashing medium pacers with no worries for straight sixes in red-ball cricket. He's toying with the bowlers,” he said.From IPL sensation to India starSooryavanshi's rise has been extraordinary. His breakthrough IPL 2026 campaign with Rajasthan Royals saw him score 776 runs in 16 matches at a staggering strike rate of 237.30, including a century and five fifties. His 72 sixes were an IPL record for a single season, while he collected the Orange Cap, Most Valuable Player, Emerging Player, Super Striker and Super Sixes awards.He subsequently became India's youngest men's international debutant during the T20I series against England. Against Zimbabwe, he scored 151 runs in three matches to help India complete a 3-0 sweep and collected his maiden Player of the Series award.His impact has also extended to age-group cricket. Earlier this year, Sooryavanshi amassed 439 runs at the ICC Under-19 World Cup and was named Player of the Tournament.The BCCI is now taking a cautious, long-term approach to his development. Secretary Devajit Saikia said the board is monitoring the teenager closely and wants his early success to translate into a career similar to those of India's past legends.“We want Vaibhav Sooryavanshi or any player of his stature to continue and serve like Sachin Tendulkar did for the country or other players who in the past became legends,” Saikia said.“So we look at Vaibhav in a very serious manner. He's monitored from every angle and every step he is taking forward in his international career. The BCCI is taking a very close look at his future.”The board's priority, Saikia stressed, is to ensure Sooryavanshi's emergence is not merely a brief burst of teenage brilliance.“You see, the BCCI can be proud that we are promoting a player of the age of 15 years who is already making his mark in the international scenario and we are very cautious that every right step he should take forward so that it should not be a one series or one year wonder,” he said.For now, though, Srikkanth sees something even bigger taking shape — a youngster whose fearless cricket is making people sit up and watch.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: No special ‘room’ for cricket: IOA draws line on BCCI’s Asian Games stay
articles.summary: Cricket News: New Delhi: If the BCCI decides its cricketers need to stay outside the official Asian Games hotels in Aichi-Nagoya, the board will have to take full r.
articles.body: New Delhi: If the BCCI decides its cricketers need to stay outside the official Asian Games hotels in Aichi-Nagoya, the board will have to take full responsibility for accommodation, food, transport and ensuring that its players reach the venue on time. The Indian Olympic Association (IOA), meanwhile, will not seek separate accommodation arrangements for cricket, as it’s for the cricket body and Organising Committee (OC) to work out an amicable solution.IOA CEO Raghuram Iyer, speaking to TOI, said the BCCI is free to make its own arrangements if the organisers’ hotels don’t suit its requirements, but the decision and the accompanying logistical responsibility would rest with the Board. The IOA, he stressed, has to ensure equal treatment and the welfare of the entire Indian contingent across 36 sports.“BCCI CEO Hemang Amin got in touch with us (IOA), and we had a fruitful discussion. They are contemplating sending an advance team to Japan to assess the facilities. The IOA is completely fine with that. Based on their assessment, they can decide whether they want to use the organisers’ facilities or make their own arrangements. It is for the BCCI and the organisers to work out the best solution. All sports, athletes, coaches and the entire delegation are treated equally by IOA,” Iyer said.For now, the Games organisers have a designated accommodation plan for both Indian teams. The men have been allotted the three-star APA Hotel Nagoya Ekimae, while the women have been assigned the four-star Meitetsu Grand Hotel, it’s been learnt. Both properties possess the requisite amenities, though they are a grade below the five-star accommodation to which India’s cricketers are generally accustomed. Rooms will be on a twin-sharing basis, another major bone of contention.The women, captained by Harmanpreet Kaur, face the first logistical test. They return from the Asia Cup in Dubai on Sept 13 and are scheduled to fly to Nagoya the following day. Their Asian Games campaign begins directly in the quarterfinals on Sept 18, with their tournament scheduled to conclude on Sept 22.The men, led by Shreyas Iyer, will travel later, leaving for Japan on Sept 21. They too enter directly at the quarterfinal stage, with their campaign running from Sept 28 and the team scheduled to return on Oct 4.With both teams having different arrival windows, the BCCI is now looking at the accommodation and logistics from its own perspective. An advance team is travelling to Japan early next week to inspect the hotels, cricket venue and other facilities before the Board takes a final call, sources revealed.The availability of suitable alternatives could be crucial. Aichi-Nagoya is already under considerable accommodation pressure, with the number of athletes and coaches expected to rise to around 17,000 from an original planning figure of 15,000. Existing hotels are being supplemented by mobile accommodation and the Costa Serena cruise ship.If the BCCI decides the official hotels do not work for its teams and opts for separate properties, it will have to arrange the entire operation, including rooms, food, local transport and travel to and from the cricket venue, while ensuring the players reach the ground well ahead of match time.That arrangement, however, would not put the cricketers outside the Games system. The BCCI would have to communicate its decision through the IOA to the organisers, and all Games-related security, accreditation and access protocols would continue to apply. Outsiders without valid accreditation would not be permitted into the team hotels.The separate stay would also have implications for anti-doping procedures. WADA and International Testing Agency (ITA) dope-control officers would have to be informed of the players’ location so that random testing can be carried out at their chosen accommodation.Iyer said the IOA was comfortable with the BCCI assessing what works best for its players.“The BCCI is taking care of its athletes, and sending an advance team is the right way to assess the facilities before making a decision. We are completely for the well-being of the athletes. Our objective is that the entire Indian delegation has a comfortable stay and a wonderful experience in Japan,” he said.The contrast with Los Angeles 2028 is already emergingWhile Japan’s cricket arrangements have prompted scrutiny, planning for cricket’s Olympic return at Los Angeles 2028 is already well advanced. Iyer was part of a joint IOA-Sports Authority of India (SAI) delegation that recently spent nearly a week in Los Angeles, meeting stakeholders and inspecting facilities across sports, including cricket.“The objective is to ensure athletes can focus only on their performance and do not face logistical issues. We are thinking well in advance about their welfare, comfort and acclimatisation, and this is something which is happening for the first time,” Iyer said.Cricket’s LA28 venue, the newly built Knight Riders Cricket Ground at the Fairplex complex in Pomona, is located next to the Sheraton Fairplex Suites & Conference Center, where the cricket teams are expected to be accommodated. Major League Cricket matches are also expected to provide an early competitive test of the new venue and playing surface.Before the Asian Games, India and Japan will also share a historic cricketing moment. Their men’s teams meet in a T20I on Sept 22 for the Suzuki Cup, marking 75 years of diplomatic relations and giving India valuable match practice ahead of the Games.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Don’t call it cricket’: Ricky Ponting makes radical T20 pitch to win over US fans
articles.summary: Cricket News: Australian great Ricky Ponting has suggested a radical change in the way cricket is marketed in the United States, saying administrators should consid.
articles.body: Australian great Ricky Ponting has suggested a radical change in the way cricket is marketed in the United States, saying administrators should consider dropping the word ‘cricket’ altogether and promoting the sport simply as ‘T20’.With the United States emerging as a key part of the International Cricket Council (ICC)’s global growth strategy, Ponting believes the traditional name could be holding the sport back in a market more familiar with baseball, American football and basketball.The former Australia captain feels the word ‘cricket’ could lead new American audiences to immediately think of Test matches and their five-day format, rather than the shorter and more entertainment-driven T20 game.Speaking to The Athletic, Ponting acknowledged that he is a traditionalist who played far more Test cricket than T20 cricket. However, he said he would be open to a complete rebranding of the format if it helped attract a new generation of American sports fans.“If I was bringing it here wholly and solely to sell and promote the game, I wouldn’t call it cricket," Ponting begins. “It’d just be rebranded as T20 only. Leave the cricket thing aside. As soon as young people hear cricket in parts of the world where they’re not brought up on the game, they think about it being a long, drawn-out, five-day game, and it’s not that."Ponting also believes baseball could provide a useful comparison for introducing T20 to an American audience. Rather than focusing on the technical differences between the sports, he wants potential fans to understand the high-scoring nature of the shortest cricket format.“I would compare it to baseball as much as I could and give kids that chance to understand you’re hitting 15 sixes per game in a game of T20 cricket, but you are hitting less than one home run a game in the game of baseball."The United States has become one of the ICC’s biggest development priorities, given the size and commercial strength of its sports market. While baseball, American football and basketball remain dominant, soccer has also been growing rapidly in the country.Cricket, meanwhile, has traditionally had a much smaller mainstream following in the US and has largely been played and followed by Asian, European and African expat communities.The ICC has been attempting to broaden that audience through a series of major initiatives. The country hosted a successful T20 World Cup in 2024, while Major League Cricket has been developed as a domestic competition. Ponting himself is involved in the league as coach of Washington Freedom.The ICC is also working towards cricket’s return to the Olympic stage at the Los Angeles 2028 Games, with efforts underway to develop suitable grounds and infrastructure in the US.With T20 at the centre of many of those efforts, Ponting believes presenting the sport as a fast-paced, modern product rather than immediately associating it with Test cricket could help the ICC connect with American audiences.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pakiatan coach explodes over King Charles report: 'Someone's just made something up'
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan's interim Test coach Mike Hesson has denied reports that Salman Ali Agha refused to attend a meeting with King Charles III, saying the story .
articles.body: Pakistan's interim Test coach Mike Hesson has denied reports that Salman Ali Agha refused to attend a meeting with King Charles III, saying the story was completely false and describing it as "unacceptable journalism."A report by UK-based The Telegraph on Thursday claimed that one of the players dropped from Pakistan's Test squad had refused to attend a meeting with the UK monarch.Hesson dismissed the report and said Salman had been informed well in advance that he would not be part of the Buckingham Palace visit.Hesson said Salman did not attend the audience with the King because he was part of the trio of players dropped from the squad first and, as a result, Salman, Imam and Rizwan were taken from the list of attendees to Clarence House, BBC reported."Look, I know there's been a void in the news, but people are just making up stories. Salman Ali Agha, as I've said, the three players were released from the squad before I arrived, well before Buckingham Palace," Hesson said on Friday."They were sent a note at that time that these three players would not be attending Buckingham Palace. So, someone's just made something up," he added.Hesson said the players who remained with the squad had already been invited to the event and there were no last-minute changes."In terms of the other players, all of the rest of the players that were in the squad were already on the list. I was already on the list as the white-ball head coach, so there have been no changes to it," he said."It was all very straightforward. Someone's just got two and two together and come up with nine. For me, that's unacceptable journalism," Hesson added.Pakistan's coaching and squad changes came after defeats in the first two Tests against England.Pakistan lost the first Test at Headingley by an innings and 103 runs before suffering a 194-run defeat at Lord's, giving England an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.The Pakistan Cricket Board then made drastic changes, sending seven players home, calling up another seven players and replacing Test head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed with Hesson, who was already serving as Pakistan's white-ball head coach.Senior players Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha, who captained Pakistan in the first Test at Headingley when Babar Azam was injured, were among the players asked to leave the tour.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Want him to become a legend’: BCCI reveals plan to nurture Vaibhav Sooryavanshi like Sachin Tendulkar
articles.summary: Cricket News: Mumbai: The BCCI is adopting a cautious route to deal with the rise of 15-year-old batting prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. The board and its key officia.
articles.body: Mumbai: The BCCI is adopting a cautious route to deal with the rise of 15-year-old batting prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi. The board and its key officials are determined to ensure his early success develops into a long and distinguished international career and does not fizzle out after a couple of years of fame and stardom.Following a Team India performance review meeting at the BCCI headquarters on Thursday, board secretary Devajit Saikia said the teenager is being closely monitored, with the board keen to nurture him along the lines of legends such as Sachin Tendulkar.“We want Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, or any player of his stature, to continue and serve like Sachin Tendulkar did for the country and become a legend. We are monitoring him from every angle and every step he takes in his international career,” Saikia said.Sooryavanshi has rapidly progressed from IPL sensation to India’s youngest men’s international debutant. He recently became the youngest player to score a Duleep Trophy fifty, hammering 92 off 81 balls, including seven sixes, for East Zone against Central Zone in Bengaluru.Making it clear that the BCCI is focused on longevity rather than instant success, Saikia added: “We are very cautious that every step he takes forward is the right one so that he does not become a one-series or one-year wonder.”Like Tendulkar, Sooryavanshi has burst onto the international scene as a teenager and quickly captured the imagination of Indian cricket fans. The left-hander earned his maiden India call-up after two sensational seasons with Rajasthan Royals.In IPL 2026, he piled up 776 runs in 16 matches at a staggering strike rate of 237.30, scoring a century and five fifties while smashing a record 72 sixes in a single season. After a slow start in England, he bounced back impressively in the T20I series against Zimbabwe, scoring 151 runs in three matches and claiming his first Player of the Series award.Asiad facilities not a concernMeanwhile, Saikia said the BCCI has no immediate concerns about accommodation or facilities for India’s cricket teams at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya.“There is no such issue which we have discussed or which is in our agenda,” he said.However, he made it clear that the board would step in if required.“If any situation arises, we will ensure our players and support staff get the best facilities. If required, the BCCI will have its own system in place to provide them.”Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Duleep Trophy final comes at right time for Mohammed Siraj to find rhythm
articles.summary: Cricket News: Chennai: The Duleep Trophy final got a boost of stardom with paceman Mohammed Siraj and left-hander Devdutt Padikkal joining the South Zone squad. For.
articles.body: Chennai: The Duleep Trophy final got a boost of stardom with paceman Mohammed Siraj and left-hander Devdutt Padikkal joining the South Zone squad. For Siraj, the domestic assignment comes at a time when questions over his form, wicket-taking impact and workload have begun to gather momentum.TOI understands that Siraj’s place came under scrutiny after the first Test against Sri Lanka in Galle, with the team management considering Gurnoor Brar for the second Test in Colombo. Siraj eventually retained his place, but in the 26 overs that he bowled in the drawn game, he could manage only two wickets.Former national selector and India opener Devang Gandhi said this is where Siraj should bring his experience into play.“I have seen Mohammed Shami from close quarters. In the second session, his pace normally used to drop, but that was often deliberate. He used to soften up the batter and then suddenly bowl that killer delivery. So when you grow a little older, it’s not always about going flat out but being judicious about it,” Gandhi said, adding that Siraj has everything in his armoury that should help him roar back.“His biggest asset is his ability to bowl with wobble seam. When a bowler does that, the ball tends to seam depending on which side of the seam it lands. That’s something he should never lose,” Gandhi added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Behavioural issues’ behind Mohammed Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq axe? Fresh details emerge from PCB shock move
articles.summary: Cricket News: The Pakistan Cricket Board’s decision to send seven players and two coaches home after defeats in the first two Tests against England continues to thr.
articles.body: The Pakistan Cricket Board’s decision to send seven players and two coaches home after defeats in the first two Tests against England continues to throw up fresh details, with behavioural concerns reportedly playing a role in the removal of senior players Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha.Pakistan suffered defeats in the opening two matches of the series, prompting the PCB to make a sweeping change ahead of the third and final Test in Edgbaston. Test coach Sarfaraz has already been replaced by Mike Hesson, while the white-ball coach will oversee the team for the final Test.Rizwan’s performances were one of the concerns surrounding the wicketkeeper-batter. He managed just 61 runs across the four innings he played and came under further criticism for his shot selection during the Lord’s Test. His reading of the game also attracted scrutiny.Imam, meanwhile, did not bat in either innings at Lord’s after suffering a calf strain. His decision not to take the field with the bat sparked questions over his commitment, with his injury becoming a major talking point.Agha’s situation was different. He captained Pakistan in the first Test in Babar’s absence but was dropped for the second match before being sent home ahead of the Edgbaston Test.According to news agency PTI, however, the decisions involving Rizwan and Imam were not linked exclusively to their performances. Behavioural issues in the dressing room were also reportedly taken into consideration.The trio of Rizwan, Imam and Agha are now expected to appear before a committee and explain their conduct in connection with certain incidents during Pakistan’s tours of the West Indies and England.The other players sent back from England were reportedly removed from the squad following Hesson’s recommendation. The interim red-ball head coach wanted to assess several white-ball specialists with whom he had previously worked.“The rest of the players sent back were done so on the recommendation of interim red-ball head coach Mike Hesson, who wanted to try out some players he had worked with in the white-ball camp,” a source said.Aaqib Javed under pressureThe latest developments are also expected to have consequences for Pakistan’s selection committee. Senior selector Aaqib Javed could be removed as part of a wider clean-up being planned by PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi.Another major development came earlier this week when selector Misbah-ul-Haq tendered his resignation. It remains unclear whether the PCB has formally accepted it.Misbah’s resignation followed the PCB issuing a show-cause notice to the selection committee. The board sought an explanation over the inclusion of Imam and Rizwan in the Test squad for the West Indies and England tours.The PCB has also issued notices to members of its selection and advisory committees, asking them to explain the decision to pick Imam and Rizwan for the England tour and the criteria used to formulate the selection policy.The shake-up could lead to a new selection committee being appointed once the England tour concludes.“A new selection committee could be announced after the England tour,” the source said.Meanwhile, Hesson could remain in charge beyond the England series. The PCB is reportedly keen to appoint him as the permanent head coach, although the move will depend on whether the New Zealander agrees to take up the role.For now, the focus remains on the fallout from the dramatic squad changes. Rizwan, Imam and Salman are expected to face a committee over their alleged behaviour, while Aaqib Javed’s position on the selection panel is also under threat as Naqvi looks to overhaul the PCB’s cricketing structure.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: More drama in Pakistan cricket: Mohsin Naqvi's PCB likely to remove chief selector Aaqib Javed in 'clean-up' exercise
articles.summary: Cricket News: Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) is likely to remove former Test cricketer and chief selector Aaqib Javed from the national selection committee as part of.
articles.body: Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) is likely to remove former Test cricketer and chief selector Aaqib Javed from the national selection committee as part of a wider "clean-up" exercise being carried out within the board, news agency PTI reported.The development comes days after senior players Mohammad Rizwan, Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha were sent home from England. The decision has raised questions over Pakistan's selection policy and team management.“Aqib is also likely to be told to focus on his role as Director Development at the Lahore High Performance Centre,” a source was quoted as saying by PTI.According to the PTI quoted source, the decision to send back Rizwan, Imam and Salman was part of the PCB's wider plan. He claimed that Rizwan and Imam were dropped not only because of their form but also because of their behaviour in the dressing room.“The rest of the players sent back were done so on the recommendation of interim red-ball head coach Mike Hesson, who wanted to try out some players he had worked with in the white-ball camp,” the source was further quoted as saying by PTI.It added that the PCB chairman Mohsin Naqvi was keen on a "clean-up" and that the selection committee could be the next area to see changes.“Aaqib, who is considered the blue-eyed boy of the chairman, is also likely to be told to just focus on his role as Director Development at the Lahore High Performance Centre,” he said.Another member of the selection committee, former Pakistan captain Misbah-ul-Haq, has already offered to step down.The PCB has also issued notices to members of the selection committee and advisory committee, asking them to explain the selection of Imam and Rizwan for the England tour and the criteria used to formulate the selection policy.Aaqib has been one of the influential figures within the PCB and has had a significant role in selection and other team-related matters.Pakistan suffered an innings and 103-run loss in the series opener at Headingley before going down by 194 runs at Lord's on Sunday as England took an unbeatable 2-0 lead in the three-match series.The Pakistan Cricket Board responded to those defeats in dramatic fashion, taking the extraordinary step of sending seven players home, calling up another seven and replacing sacked Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed with Hesson, already Pakistan's white-ball boss.Senior players Imam-ul-Haq and Salman Ali Agha, who was Pakistan's captain at Headingley when Babar Azam was injured, were among those told to leave.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘CSK captaincy must be changed’: Sanju Samson backed to take over from Ruturaj Gaikwad
articles.summary: Cricket News: Chennai Super Kings have built their reputation on stability, but the franchise could be forced to make some major calls ahead of the 2027 Indian Prem.
articles.body: Chennai Super Kings have built their reputation on stability, but the franchise could be forced to make some major calls ahead of the 2027 Indian Premier League season.The five-time champions have endured a difficult phase, missing out on the playoffs for three successive seasons. Their 2026 campaign was further complicated by skipper Ruturaj Gaikwad’s struggles with the bat, while the arrival of Sanju Samson from Rajasthan Royals sparked debate over whether CSK could consider a leadership change.Although CSK have traditionally avoided knee-jerk decisions, former India batter Sadagoppan Ramesh has now backed Samson to take over the captaincy if the franchise decides to move on from Gaikwad.Samson brings considerable leadership experience from his time at Rajasthan Royals. The wicketkeeper-batter, who was named Player of the Tournament at the 2026 T20 World Cup, moved to CSK ahead of the 2026 IPL and finished the season as the franchise’s highest run-scorer.Ramesh believes those credentials make Samson a serious option for CSK."CSK are seemingly considering many options for the captaincy and even wondering whether a change is needed. Sanju Samson should be considered as captain because he’s such a fantastic team player. The CSK captaincy must be changed, and if it is, CSK must seriously consider Sanju Samson,” said Ramesh on his Instagram handle.He also pointed to Samson’s IPL captaincy record, while stressing that changing the skipper alone would not solve all of CSK’s problems.“Samson has also captained 66 matches in the IPL and won 33. So he has a 50% success rate. Under him, RR performed well, reaching the final and making another playoff appearance. Of course, CSK need several other things to change, and just making Sanju the captain won’t win them the trophy. But if at all they change captains, Sanju must be strongly considered,” he added.Gaikwad’s difficult 2026 seasonGaikwad’s position has come under scrutiny following a disappointing campaign in 2026.The right-hander scored 337 runs at an average of 28.08 and also recorded the lowest strike rate among all batters during the powerplay. His struggles added to the questions surrounding CSK’s leadership ahead of the next season.Ramesh is not the first former CSK player to suggest that Gaikwad could benefit from stepping away from the captaincy.Former CSK and India batter Subramaniam Badrinath had previously argued that Gaikwad should be relieved of leadership duties and allowed to concentrate entirely on his batting.“So once you remove him from captaincy, he’ll perform well as a batter. It won’t be a harsh decision if he is stripped of captaincy. It’s more beneficial for the player and the franchise. It’ll only do Gaikwad a world of good. This is not new to him alone. Even greats like Sachin Tendulkar have been affected by captaincy. If you are someone who is intense and thinks too much, it’s hard to detach from captaincy even while batting,” he had said on his YouTube channel.CSK themselves have several decisions to make before the 2027 season. The franchise are currently looking for a new head coach after Stephen Fleming stepped down earlier this year.There is also uncertainty surrounding MS Dhoni’s future, with it still unclear whether the former India captain will continue playing for CSK in the 2027 IPL.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Shubman Gill joins Fazilka Falcons, set to make Sher-E-Punjab T20 League 2026 debut
articles.summary: Cricket News: Shubman Gill has joined the Fazilka Falcons squad for the ongoing Sher-E-Punjab T20 League 2026, giving the side a major boost after a difficult start.
articles.body: Shubman Gill has joined the Fazilka Falcons squad for the ongoing Sher-E-Punjab T20 League 2026, giving the side a major boost after a difficult start to the tournament.The India Test and ODI captain was seen preparing with the Falcons in a video shared by the franchise on Instagram, signalling his arrival ahead of his first appearance in the competition.Gill is among a select group of India stars featuring in the Punjab T20 League this season. He is joined by fellow opening batter Abhishek Sharma and India pacer Arshdeep Singh, who are also part of the high-profile domestic tournament.The Fazilka Falcons have already played three matches this season, but Gill has missed all three. Sanvir Singh has led the team in his absence.The Falcons have managed just one win from their opening three games, suffering two defeats in the process. They currently sit fifth in the six-team Punjab T20 League 2026 points table and will be hoping Gill's arrival can help turn their campaign around.Gill's availability comes after a hectic international schedule. The 26-year-old is India's captain in Tests and ODIs but is currently not part of the T20I team, giving him an opportunity to return to the shortest format through the Punjab league.His last T20 appearance came during IPL 2026, when he produced a strong campaign for Gujarat Titans. Gill scored 732 runs in 16 matches at an average of 45.75 and a strike rate of 196.22, with a highest score of 104.Gill's performances helped Gujarat Titans reach the IPL 2026 final, although they eventually finished runners-up after losing to Royal Challengers Bengaluru.With the Fazilka Falcons struggling near the bottom of the table, Gill's arrival could prove significant as they look to revive their campaign in the remainder of the Sher-E-Punjab T20 League.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Nothing left for the bowlers’: Suresh Raina sounds alarm over IPL impact player rule
articles.summary: Cricket News: Suresh Raina has become the latest former India cricketer to raise concerns over the impact player rule in the Indian Premier League (IPL), arguing th.
articles.body: Suresh Raina has become the latest former India cricketer to raise concerns over the impact player rule in the Indian Premier League (IPL), arguing that the experiment has significantly tilted the balance of the game towards batters.The former Chennai Super Kings (CSK) batter, who was part of four IPL-winning campaigns, believes bowlers have been particularly disadvantaged since the rule was introduced in 2023. The issue has remained a talking point among players, with Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma also expressing their reservations about the rule during the 2024 season.Raina says impact player rule has made life difficult for bowlersThe impact player rule allows teams to name five substitute options after the toss, from which they can bring in one replacement at any point during the match. The teams first announce their batting and bowling XIs at the toss, while the designated replacement can be introduced after the first ball has been bowled.Raina believes the additional substitution option has played a major role in the explosion of batting in the IPL. Scores that once appeared difficult to chase have increasingly become achievable, with teams regularly crossing the 200-run mark and several 250-plus totals being recorded over the last three seasons.The trend was particularly evident during the 2024 edition, when Punjab Kings successfully chased down a target of more than 260 against Kolkata Knight Riders.Raina feels the growing emphasis on batting depth has left bowlers with fewer opportunities to influence matches.“I am against the Impact player rule. A lot of fit players also bat and just sit down. How will you improve? There is no such rule in the World Cup. I understand the entertainment factor, but there is nothing left for the bowlers. Earlier, 170 was a competitive score, but now 250 is being chased as well. Even 300 is being scored," Raina told the former India batter, Aakash Chopra.The former India international believes the rule has also reduced the consequences of losing wickets, as teams can bring in another specialist batter when required."Leave something for the bowlers. There is no wicket-taking option. The batters don't get out, and with extra batters, there will be pressure on the bowlers,” he added.Raina changes stance on Indian players in overseas leaguesRaina also addressed another long-standing debate surrounding Indian cricketers: whether they should be permitted to participate in overseas T20 leagues.The former India batter, who was part of India's 2011 World Cup-winning team, said he no longer believes there is a need for Indian players to feature in competitions such as Australia's Big Bash League (BBL) and England's Hundred.Raina revealed that he had previously been keen on playing in overseas leagues and had even come close to doing so. However, permission was not granted at the time.“I feel Indian players should not be allowed now. Our league has become very big. When we used to go on Australia and England tours before, I used to ask this. I had come close to playing as well, but then they said no," said Raina.'We are ruling the world': Raina backs IPL's standingAccording to Raina, the situation has changed considerably since those days. The IPL has grown into one of the biggest competitions in world cricket, while overseas leagues have increasingly relied on international players travelling to India for the tournament.He also feels the overall quality of some foreign T20 leagues has declined compared to the past, making it even less important for Indian players to gain experience abroad."Now, a lot of outside players come here, and the quality of foreign leagues has also gone down. Back then, I would have definitely said yes. But at this time, we are ruling the world. Cricket is going somewhere else, and our team is very solid,” he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: ‘Babar Azam the next target?’: Ex-Pakistan captain launches scathing attack on PCB over England Test chaos
articles.summary: Cricket News: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) is facing renewed criticism over its handling of the senior men's national team, with former captain Rashid Latif acc.
articles.body: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) is facing renewed criticism over its handling of the senior men's national team, with former captain Rashid Latif accusing the board of effectively running the side through “remote control” and questioning why coaches and captains are not being given greater authority.The latest criticism comes after the PCB made an unprecedented mid-series overhaul, sending seven players and two coaches back to Pakistan following defeats in the first two Tests against England.The sweeping changes have added to the uncertainty surrounding Pakistan's Test set-up, with several former players and prominent voices in the game questioning the timing and scale of the PCB's decision.Rashid Latif questions PCB's handling of coachesPakistan had already been under considerable pressure after losing the opening two Tests against England. However, rather than retaining the same group for the remainder of the series, the PCB opted for a major reshuffle.Among those sent home were senior players Mohammad Rizwan and Salman Ali Agha. Test coach Sarfaraz Ahmed was also removed from the set-up, with white-ball coach Mike Hesson taking charge for the third and final Test in Birmingham.Latif has now questioned why Sarfaraz and bowling coach Umar Gul were sent to the UK in the first place if the PCB intended to exercise such a high degree of control over the team.Taking to X, the former Pakistan captain also referred to the departures of Jason Gillespie and Gary Kirsten, both of whom previously stepped down after disagreements over the level of authority and freedom available to them.Latif also brought captain Babar Azam into the discussion, suggesting that if the captain was not following the team's preferred direction, the PCB should have removed him rather than sending coaches back home."If the team had to be run by remote control, then why were Sarfaraz and Umar Gul sent? Why were the selection powers taken away from Gary Kirsten and Jason Gillespie? And if captain Babar Azam wasn’t listening, the captain should have been sacked — so why were Sarfaraz and Umar Gul sent back instead? Is Babar Azam the next target?” Latif wrote on X.PCB faces backlash over seven-player overhaulThe PCB's decision to make such sweeping changes in the middle of a Test series has attracted criticism from several high-profile figures in Pakistan cricket.Michael Atherton, Nasser Hussain, Ramiz Raja, Basit Ali and Shahid Afridi have all questioned the move, with the critics arguing that such drastic changes could create even more instability within an already struggling Pakistan side.The PCB, however, has defended its decision.Chairman Mohsin Naqvi previously backed the overhaul, insisting that the board had taken the harsh step because it believed it was necessary for the betterment of the team.Pakistan's Test struggles continueThe dramatic changes come against the backdrop of Pakistan's prolonged struggles in the longest format.Pakistan are currently at the bottom of the World Test Championship (WTC) standings and have never been genuine contenders for a place in the WTC final during the current cycle.The latest campaign will also mark the fourth consecutive WTC cycle in which Pakistan finish in the bottom half of the standings, highlighting the extent of their problems in Test cricket.The defeat in England has only intensified the scrutiny surrounding the team's direction and the PCB's decision-making process.Another captaincy change under scrutinyPakistan's Test leadership has also undergone another change this year.Earlier in 2026, the PCB replaced Shan Masood with Babar Azam as Test captain after Bangladesh completed a 2-0 series victory over Pakistan.Babar's return to the leadership role initially brought some stability, with Pakistan drawing their two-Test series against the West Indies.However, the team's fortunes quickly deteriorated once the side arrived in England. After losing the opening two Tests, the PCB responded with a drastic squad overhaul, sending seven players and two members of the coaching staff home.That decision has now prompted fresh questions over who is actually making the key decisions within Pakistan cricket, with Latif's comments adding another layer to the growing controversy surrounding the board's handling of the national team.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Those two little pals of mine': Sonny Ramadhin became first Indian-origin cricketer to play for West Indies in 1950, helped them beat England in England for the first time. He became part of first great West Indies team and a protagonist of one of cricket's most iconic songs
articles.summary: Cricket News: Sonny Ramadhin became the first cricketer of Indian origin to represent the West Indies when he made his Test debut at Old Trafford during the 1950 to.
articles.body: Sonny Ramadhin became the first cricketer of Indian origin to represent the West Indies when he made his Test debut at Old Trafford during the 1950 tour of England.Born in St Charles Village in Trinidad, not far from the capital Port of Spain, Ramadhin lost both his parents when he was a toddler. He was raised by his grandparents, who had migrated from India to work on one of Trinidad's cocoa estates.Ramadhin did not have a first name when he was born. He was simply called "boy" during his childhood. Over time, that became "Sonny", and the name stayed with him.Then something unusual happened during the 1950 tour of England. In Ramadhin's own words: "When I got to England they insisted that nobody could go through life without initials. The next time I picked up the paper I'd become KT Ramadhin. I never did find out what my new English names were supposed to be!"No matter what the English newspapers called him, he remained Sonny Ramadhin — the mystery spinner from the Caribbean who made the cricket world take notice in 1950.The spin twins Ramadhin and fellow spinner Alf Valentine became one of the biggest reasons behind West Indies' famous 3-1 Test series win over England in 1950. It was the first time the West Indies defeated England in England in a Test series.What made their story even more remarkable was their lack of experience. Before the England tour, both Ramadhin and Valentine had played only two first-class matches each — both trial games for selection.England had prepared for the famous Three Ws — Frank Worrell, Everton Weekes and Clyde Walcott — who formed the backbone of West Indies' batting. What England had not prepared for was a pair of spinners with completely different styles.Ramadhin was famous for bowling both off-breaks and leg-breaks with almost no visible change in his action. Valentine bowled left-arm orthodox spin.Test debut at Old TraffordRamadhin and Valentine made their Test debuts together in the first Test at Old Trafford, Manchester, on June 8, 1950.West Indies lost that match by 202 runs, even though the pitch offered plenty of help for spin bowlers. Together, Ramadhin and Valentine took 15 wickets in the match, but England's spin trio of Jim Laker, Eric Hollies and Bob Berry used the conditions better.The defeat, however, was only the beginning of a historic series.Lords of Lord'sThe second Test at Lord's became one of the most iconic matches in West Indies cricket history. West Indies scored 326 in the first innings, thanks largely to Allan Rae's century. Ramadhin and Valentine then bowled England out for just 151.West Indies declared their second innings at 425 for 6 and set England a target of 601 runs.At the start of the final day — a Thursday — there were very few spectators at Lord's. Most of them were West Indians, and there were fewer than 100 in the crowd.England resumed at 281 for 4, chasing what was almost an impossible target.By lunch they had lost five more wickets. Shortly after 2.18 pm, Johnny Wardle was trapped lbw by Frank Worrell, and West Indies completed a 326-run victory, their first Test win over England in England. Ramadhin was the star of the match.He finished with figures of 5 for 66 in the first innings and 6 for 86 in the second. Valentine supported him with figures of 4 for 48 and 3 for 79.West Indies went on to win the remaining two Tests as well — by 10 wickets at Nottingham and by an innings and 56 runs at The Oval — to seal the series 3-1.Those two little pals of mine ...The victory at Lord's was iconic. But more iconic were the celebrations that followed.A small group of West Indian supporters ran onto the field carrying "guitar-like instruments", according to The Times. They danced, sang calypsos and created music using dustbin lids and even a carving knife scraped across a cheese grater.Among those supporters were Lord Kitchener and Lord Beginner, who had arrived in Britain aboard the Empire Windrush in 1948 as part of the first major wave of Caribbean immigrants.Lord Kitchener had been singing calypsos throughout the Test match. After the victory, he came up with lines that celebrated the heroes of the day:Walcott, Weekes and Worrell held up their nameWith wonder shots throughout the gameBut England was beaten clean out of timeWith the spin bowling of Ramadhin and Valentine.Those lines eventually became part of Cricket, Lovely Cricket, one of the most famous songs associated with West Indies cricket.There has been some confusion over who actually wrote the song. It was recorded and released by Lord Beginner, but there's some strong evidence to suggest that it was created jointly by Lord Beginner and Lord Kitchener.Former Southwark mayor Sam King, who was present at Lord's that day, recalled the moment in a 1998 interview with The Guardian."I was about going home, about 20 voices said, Sam, you can't go home, man. Kitchener going to make a song.' I said, What?' They said, Just come.' We sat down on the grass and Kitchener says, Cricket, lovely cricket,' and someone said, Put Ramadhin in, man.' And he put Ramadhin in, and he went over it, and in 30 minutes he wrote the song, Cricket, lovely cricket, at Lord's, where I saw it. Yardley won the toss, but Goddard won the Test, with those little pals of mine, Ramadhin and Valentine.' I was there. That was history."Whether it was written by one person or together, Cricket, Lovely Cricket became part of West Indies cricket folklore. The first stanza of calypso reads:Cricket lovely Cricket,At Lord's where I saw it;Cricket lovely Cricket,At Lord's where I saw it;Yardley tried his bestBut Goddard won the test.They gave the crowd plenty fun;Second Test and West Indies won. With those two little pals of mine, Ramadhin and Valentine.More than a one-series wonderRamadhin remained one of West Indies' mainstay through the 1950s. He was the leading wicket-taker in the 1953-54 home series against England, taking 23 wickets at an average of 24. Two years later, in New Zealand, he picked up 20 wickets at an average of 15.When West Indies returned to England in 1957, Ramadhin was still their biggest bowling weapon.In the first Test at Edgbaston, he produced the best innings figures of his Test career, 7 for 49. During one spell after lunch, he took 6 wickets for just 9 runs in eight overs.However, England responded tactically in the second innings.Peter May and Colin Cowdrey repeatedly stretched forward, using their pads to smother Ramadhin's spin because they believed lbw decisions would not be given.With two West Indies bowlers injured, captain John Goddard kept Ramadhin bowling almost continuously. Ramadhin bowled 98 overs in that innings, which remains a Test cricket record. Despite many appeals, the umpires didn't give any lbw in that innings.Ramadhin later became eligible to play county cricket after settling in England, and joined Lancashire in 1964.He also played Minor Counties cricket for Lincolnshire into his early forties and continued playing league cricket until he was nearly 50.After representing Lancashire and spending years in the Lancashire leagues as a professional, he settled permanently in north-west England following his retirement.He died on February 26, 2022, at the age of 92. A star of his time, Ramadhin, the first Indian to play for West Indies, claimed 158 wickets from 43 Tests during a 10-year international career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Age is just a number': Ishan Kishan confident of 'hungry' Mohammed Shami making India comeback
articles.summary: Cricket News: At 36, Mohammed Shami may be closer to the twilight of his career than its peak, but his desire to return to India colours remains as strong as ever. .
articles.body: At 36, Mohammed Shami may be closer to the twilight of his career than its peak, but his desire to return to India colours remains as strong as ever. That is the belief of East Zone captain Ishan Kishan, who has seen first-hand the veteran pacer’s determination during their run to the Duleep Trophy final.Shami, who has 903 wickets from 100 first-class matches, produced a match-winning spell in the semifinal against Central Zone in Bengaluru. For Kishan, however, it is not just Shami's performances that stand out, it is the hunger behind them.“I think he is just one of the best. He has been a legend of this game. He has been doing so well since he started playing for Bengal. He has been picking wickets, giving all his energy and he has done so well for the Indian cricket team also,” Kishan said at the pre-match press conference.While Shami is nearing the latter stages of his career, Kishan believes age should not be a barrier if the pacer continues to maintain his work ethic and hunger.“I feel age is just a number. If he is working hard it doesn't matter. I see that hunger in Shami bhai because who better than me to judge about hunger right now,” Kishan said, referring to his own period away from the Indian team.“Looking at his efforts as a captain, I felt very nice, because Shami bhai came in, asking me for those extra overs to get the wickets. This is something which always gives confidence to skippers. When you have bowlers who are willing to get you wickets, it's always good to have him in the team,” Kishan said.Shami even chipped in with the bat, striking two boundaries, prompting Kishan to jokingly label him an all-rounder.“He also finished with two boundaries, so he is an all-rounder I feel nowadays. So I am very happy to have him in my team,” he added.East Zone eye first Duleep Trophy title in 13 yearsEast Zone will take on South Zone in the Duleep Trophy final from Sunday, with a chance to lift the prestigious trophy for the first time since the 2012-13 season. East Zone defeated Central Zone in the semifinal to reach the final after 13 years. Their last title came in 2012-13, when they beat Central Zone to win their second Duleep Trophy.South Zone, meanwhile, are among the most successful teams in the competition, having won the title 12 times, with their most recent triumph coming in 2023. The final at Chepauk will also bring several India internationals and current white-ball stars together before the focus shifts to international cricket.Mohammed Siraj and Devdutt Padikkal have joined South Zone after featuring in India's recent 1-0 Test series victory over Sri Lanka, although KL Rahul is not expected to play the final.T20I specialists Tilak Varma, Ishan Kishan and Vaibhav Sooryavanshi have also been cleared by the BCCI to feature despite India's upcoming T20I series against Afghanistan, beginning September 13. Tilak will captain South Zone, while Kishan will lead East Zone, with Sooryavanshi serving as his deputy.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.
